assumptions: Counts are negative binomial; the gene-level test is the exact conditional test on the two groups' totals, not a normal approximation.
`exact` holds every prognostic gene at one average count and one dispersion unless `counts` and `dispersions` are given; `average_power` lets each gene's log-fold-change vary, drawn from a normal.
The per-gene α is derived from the FDR as m1·power·f / ((m − m1)(1 − f)), which is the FDR-to-α step both packages use.
limits: `exact` solves power on a whole-percent grid, so a power it returns is quantised to 0.01 — that is upstream's resolution, not a rounding here.
`average_power` reaches its answer through a minimizer whose critical value is pinned to about 1e-3; the sample size it returns is exact, the power behind it to about 2e-7.
A dispersion estimated from a small pilot is itself uncertain, and the answer is more sensitive to it than to the fold change.
Power by simulating whole experiments through edgeR, stratified by expression, is simulate_rnaseq_power's; ssizeRNA's own voom/limma simulation wrapper is not ported.
bio.jane/contract.question: For an RNA-seq experiment testing thousands of genes at a target false discovery rate, how many biological replicates per group are needed, and what power does a given number give?

description: How many biological replicates an RNA-seq experiment needs when the question is about the WHOLE experiment rather than one gene: the exact negative-binomial test with the per-gene α derived from a target false discovery rate across m genes of which m1 are expected to move (RnaSeqSampleSize 2.23.0, Zhao et al. 2018; the test is Robinson & Smyth 2008's, edgeR's exactTest), or the AVERAGE power across genes whose effects differ, with the FDR controlled (ssizeRNA 1.3.3, Bi & Liu 2016). Give `solve_for` n to size the experiment or power to score a design. With `counts` and `dispersions` from a pilot, the power is computed per gene over that real distribution rather than for one idealised gene. Unlike calculate_rnaseq_power this makes no normal approximation, so it is the one to use at small n or low counts.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

count.description: λ₀, the average read count for a prognostic gene in the control group. Only applies when method is exact.

counts.description: a pilot's average read count per gene. With `dispersions`, the power is computed for each of these genes and averaged, instead of for one idealised gene. Only applies when method is exact.

dispersion.description: φ₀, the negative-binomial dispersion of a prognostic gene — the square of the biological coefficient of variation. Only applies when method is exact.

dispersions.description: the dispersion of each gene in `counts`, in the same order. Only applies when method is exact.

effect_mean.description: the mean of the normal each gene's true log-fold-change is drawn from. Only applies when method is average_power.

effect_sd.description: the spread of those true effects ACROSS genes; 0 would make every gene identical. Only applies when method is average_power.

fdr.description: the false discovery rate to control across the experiment.

fold_change.description: ρ, the minimum fold change to detect in a prognostic gene. Only applies when method is exact.

m.description: genes tested. Only applies when method is exact.

m1.description: genes expected to be differentially expressed. Only applies when method is exact.

max_n.description: the largest replicate count to search. Only applies when method is average_power. Advanced.

method.description: which question. `exact` powers one prognostic gene with the exact negative-binomial test at an α derived from the FDR; `average_power` asks what the mean power across genes is when each gene's effect is drawn from a normal. Values: exact (Exact negative-binomial test), average_power (Average power across genes).

n.description: biological replicates in the control group, when solving power. Only applies when solve_for is power.

normalization_ratio.description: w, the ratio of the two groups' normalization factors. Only applies when method is exact. Advanced.

pi0.description: the proportion of genes with no effect. A list asks the question once per proportion, which is how the answer's sensitivity to it is read. Only applies when method is average_power.

power.description: the power to reach, when solving n.

sigma.description: the common within-gene standard deviation on that scale. Only applies when method is average_power.

size_ratio.description: k, the ratio of treatment to control group size. Only applies when method is exact. Advanced.

solve_for.description: size the experiment, or score a design you already have. Values: n (Replicates per group), power (Power).

name: plan_rnaseq_experiment

alpha.description: the per-gene α the FDR target implies

curve.description: power against replicates, which is the plot this question is read from

method.description: which of the two questions was answered

n.description: replicates per group (the control group, when the groups differ)

perGene.description: the power of each gene in `counts`, when a pilot distribution was given

power.description: the power that number of replicates gives

rCall.description: the R call that reproduces the answer

rows.description: each (n, power) the search evaluated, one row per n in n order, or every (pi0, n, power) for average power
